documents.unit: Division of Undergraduate Learning (Undergraduate Academic Processes Team)
documents.title: Guidance: Addressing Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity
documents.summary: October 2025 guidance from the Undergraduate Academic Processes Team to instructors on handling AI and academic integrity. It sets no AI rule itself, requires a syllabus AI policy, and offers preventative (clear expectations, assignment redesign) and reactive (evidence beyond detectors, conversation first) advice.
documents.stance_why: The document tells instructors that "your course AI policy is a required component of your syllabus" and offers tips; it never bans or permits AI itself, so it delegates the decision to instructors.

units.why: The guidance says "expectations placed on our students post-graduation suggest that the ethical and effective use of AI must now be an important college learning outcome"; it justifies teaching AI use as a professional skill, so P44 (the claim is about learning outcomes, informs).
units.anchor: the ethical and effective use of AI must now be an important college learning outcome

units.why: States the integrity concern that frames the guidance: tools "challenge traditional definitions of academic originality and authorship, especially when they are used without transparency". It is a purpose/principle statement, so P56 rather than a disclosure rule.
units.anchor: challenge traditional definitions of academic originality and authorship, especially when they are used without transparency

units.why: Directly says "your course AI policy is a required component of your syllabus", an obligation on instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus: P09.
units.anchor: your course AI policy is a required component of your syllabus

units.why: Advises instructors to repeat expectations "on the actual assignments or exams" so they are front and center; it is about communicating expectations (P09), optional so modality is may.
units.anchor: repeating or referencing these expectations and limits on the actual assignments or exams

units.why: Suggests instructors share their own AI use with students ("If you use AI for anything, sharing this example"), which fits P47 (instructor discloses own use); recommended not required, so should.
units.anchor: If you use AI for anything, sharing this example can further emphasize to students

units.why: Tells instructors to explain how classroom limits on AI "support students in their current and future success"; it asks instructors to give the learning rationale for limits, so P41 (limits justified by learning), not P44.
units.anchor: Explain how the limits that you place on the use of AI in the classroom

units.why: Asks instructors to check whether limits "apply in a post-graduation professional context" and use that as a reason for the limits; this links classroom rules to professional practice, so P44 over P41.
units.anchor: limits you are imposing also likely to apply in a post- graduation professional context

units.why: Instructs faculty to "Point students to AI Literacy resources that teach them about appropriate uses of AI"; this is teaching AI use as a skill (P44), not faculty training (P63).
units.anchor: Point students to AI Literacy resources that teach them about appropriate uses of AI

units.why: States that assessments can be "less compatible with generative AI problem-solving", the basis for the assignment-redesign advice that follows: P35.
units.anchor: design assessments that are less compatible with generative AI problem- solving

units.why: A listed tip, "Assess intermediate stages of work", is a redesign of grading around process: P35.
units.anchor: Assess intermediate stages of work.

units.why: Tip to "Assess student reflections on the process"; the instructor is redesigning assessment (P35), though reflections (P26) also fit. P35 chosen because the instruction is addressed to the assessor, not a student submission duty.
units.anchor: Assess student reflections on the process of completing the assignment.

units.why: Recommends building AI into the assignment so students "critically analyze and evaluate the output"; an assignment redesign around AI (P35) that also builds verification.
units.anchor: Integrate AI into the assignment by asking students to critically analyze and evaluate

units.why: Suggests assignments tied to "each student's individual past experiences" or in-class discussions that AI has difficulty with; redesign of assignments around AI: P35.
units.anchor: assignments that are based on each student’s individual past experiences

units.why: Recommends an "oral defense" component, a way to check understanding by having students explain their work: P34.
units.anchor: Create assignments that have an ‘oral defense’ component to them

units.why: Adds that written assignments can "require students to submit their version history"; students submit drafts as process evidence, so P26.
units.anchor: require students to submit their version history with the assignment

units.why: Says to "Provide in-class/proctored assignments when appropriate", shifting weight to proctored, unassisted work: P33.
units.anchor: Provide in-class/proctored assignments when appropriate.

units.why: Offered as a step to reduce "the pressures to cheat"; it is a prevention measure through support, and no type covers reducing cheating pressure, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Encourage and periodically remind students to visit you during your office hours
units.uncovered_note: Instructor steps that reduce student pressure to cheat (office hours, advisor referrals, time-management resources) as an integrity prevention strategy.

units.why: Directs instructors to "Teach students ethical and appropriate uses of AI" as an integrity measure; teaching AI use as a skill: P44.
units.anchor: Teach students ethical and appropriate uses of AI.

units.why: Says that unauthorized AI work submitted as one's own can lead to "a formal academic integrity violation charge"; it classifies the misuse as an integrity matter handled by the integrity process: P36.
units.anchor: we can move forward with a formal academic integrity violation charge

units.why: States detectors "are not reliable enough or transparent enough to be the only evidence" and hearing boards look for more than detector results: P39.
units.anchor: such detectors are not reliable enough or transparent enough to be the only evidence

units.why: Lists evidence of unauthorized AI use instead of detector results, here "references that do not exist"; evidence used to identify misuse: P40.
units.anchor: Clear hallucinations in the assignment, such as references that do not exist

units.why: Second evidence item, "material that was not part of the course" that suggests an AI source; used to identify misuse: P40.
units.anchor: Inclusion of material that was not part of the course

units.why: Third evidence item, "distinct 'voices' in a single assignment"; process/style evidence to identify misuse: P40.
units.anchor: Identifying distinct “voices” in a single assignment

units.why: Fourth evidence item, "abruptly terminated or oddly formatted" text; evidence to identify misuse: P40.
units.anchor: Sentences or paragraphs that are abruptly terminated or oddly formatted.

units.why: Detector results may start "a constructive (rather than punitive) conversation" with the student before any charge; talking with the student first: P57.
units.anchor: useful in starting a constructive (rather than punitive) conversation between you and the student

units.why: Advises opening the conversation with "genuine curiosity rather than a means to extract a confession"; how to talk with the student before escalating: P57.
units.anchor: questions that are based in genuine curiosity rather than a means to extract a confession

documents.title: Generative AI Guidelines
documents.summary: University-wide generative AI guidelines mostly about data protection, approved tools, verification and transparency. For coursework it defers to the syllabus and instructor, and forbids submitting unauthorized AI-generated work as one's own.
documents.stance_why: The coursework section says "Follow your course syllabus/instructor rules on whether and how AI may be used" and tells instructors to make expectations explicit; no single AI stance is set, so the document delegates.

units.why: Opening purpose statement: all community members are "responsible for protecting University information and complying with University policies" when using AI; a framework statement of purpose: P56.
units.anchor: responsible for protecting University information and complying with University policies, legal obligations and ethical standards

units.why: Defines generative AI as "systems that can create or transform content", setting what the guidelines cover: P61.
units.anchor: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) refers to systems that can create or transform content

units.why: Places the guidelines in a hierarchy from university policy to department to course-specific requirements, "with more specific requirements taking precedence"; a framework of scope (P56). P04 not chosen because it does not say instructors decide AI permission.
units.anchor: more specific requirements taking precedence as applicable

units.why: Scope statement: applies to faculty, staff, students and affiliates for "University work or coursework", on any device; defines policy scope: P61.
units.anchor: These guidelines apply to Clemson University faculty, staff, students, contractors and affiliates

units.why: Core principle "Protect Clemson data" with data classification deciding what may be entered; data protection: P50.
units.anchor: Use data classification to decide what can be entered into an AI system

units.why: Principle to "Prefer Clemson-approved services" which are reviewed; prefer vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: Prefer Clemson-approved services for University work.

units.why: Core principle: "Assume outputs can be wrong. Verify AI-generated information"; verification duty: P31.
units.anchor: Assume outputs can be wrong. Verify AI-generated information using authoritative sources.

units.why: Principle "Be transparent": disclose and cite AI use "when required" by instructor or others; disclosure with a submission: P24.
units.anchor: Disclose and cite AI use when required by your instructor, publisher, sponsor

units.why: Principle "You remain responsible": users are "accountable for decisions, work products and outcomes produced with AI assistance"; ownership of what one submits or produces: P29.
units.anchor: You are accountable for decisions, work products and outcomes produced with AI assistance.

units.why: Requires users to check the data and tool matrix before using any AI tool to see whether use is "permitted, requires prior approval, or is prohibited"; data protection and vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: determine the applicable data classification and tool category, and consult this matrix

units.why: Risk description: "prompts, uploads and outputs may be stored for a period of time"; data privacy fact: P50.
units.anchor: prompts, uploads and outputs may be stored for a period of time

units.why: States tools "can generate incorrect, fabricated or misleading content" including code behavior; AI output may be wrong: P31.
units.anchor: AI tools can generate incorrect, fabricated or misleading content

units.why: Legal risk that outputs "may incorporate or resemble copyrighted or proprietary content": P52.
units.anchor: AI outputs may incorporate or resemble copyrighted or proprietary content.

units.why: Says AI use "may create plagiarism or authorship issues if not disclosed or permitted", treating undisclosed or unpermitted use as a plagiarism problem: P36.
units.anchor: AI use may create plagiarism or authorship issues if not disclosed or permitted.

units.why: Names bias and privacy harms as ethical risks of AI use: P53.
units.anchor: Some uses can introduce bias, privacy harms or misuse of sensitive information.

units.why: Checklist rule: "If any of the information above is unclear: do not enter the data"; data protection: P50 (P10 asks about permission in a course, not data).
units.anchor: If any of the information above is unclear: do not enter the data.

units.why: Best practice: "Enter only public data into unapproved/public AI tools": P50.
units.anchor: Enter only public data into unapproved/public AI tools.

units.why: Best practice banning pasting of passwords, tokens and keys into AI tools: P50.
units.anchor: Never paste secrets. Do not include passwords, access tokens, private keys

units.why: Says to "record the tool used, date and what was asked" for important work; this names tool, date and prompt details to record: P25.
units.anchor: record the tool used, date and what was asked

units.why: Tells users to evaluate outputs for bias and disparate impact; output must be critically checked, so P31 rather than P53 (which only names concerns).
units.anchor: Audit outputs, as they may reflect bias or unfair assumptions.

units.why: Rule of thumb banning unreviewed connectors/plugins on University systems; prefer vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: Do not enable connectors/plugins for University systems unless they are reviewed and approved

units.why: Third-party meeting bots "should never be used with sensitive data unless explicitly reviewed and approved"; vetted-tool and data rule: P50.
units.anchor: should never be used with sensitive data unless explicitly reviewed and approved

units.why: Listed as "Allowed / Generally Low Risk": AI as a support tool for "brainstorming, outlining, grammar improvement". Brainstorming is the lead use, so P15 (P18 for prose is secondary).
units.anchor: Using AI as a support tool (brainstorming, outlining, grammar improvement of your own writing)

units.why: Under "Use With Caution": drafting graded content "only if permitted and properly disclosed". This sets permission as the condition, so P06-style fallback rather than P24.
units.anchor: Drafting content that will be evaluated or graded (only if permitted and properly disclosed)

units.why: Listed as "Prohibited / High Risk": submitting AI-generated work as your own "when not explicitly permitted"; students may not have AI produce submitted work: P19.
units.anchor: Submitting AI-generated or ghostwritten work as your own for graded assignments when not explicitly permitted

units.why: Students are told to follow "course syllabus/instructor rules on whether and how AI may be used"; instructors set the rule: P04.
units.anchor: Follow your course syllabus/instructor rules

units.why: Student rule in the Academic Work section: "Do not submit AI-generated work as your own when it is not authorized": P19.
units.anchor: Do not submit AI-generated work as your own when it is not authorized.

units.why: When AI is allowed students must "be prepared to Describe your process"; students explain what they did: P30.
units.anchor: Describe your process
units.policy: When AI use is allowed, students are prepared to describe their process.

units.why: Instructors "Make AI expectations explicit in syllabi and assignment instructions"; a syllabus statement requirement: P09.
units.anchor: Make AI expectations explicit in syllabi and assignment instructions

units.why: Instructors are told to "Consider whether students may" brainstorm, get feedback, generate code snippets or summarize; the choice is left to each instructor: P04.
units.anchor: Consider whether students may:

units.why: Research rule banning unpublished or sponsor-restricted information in public tools; AI in research and scholarship: P62.
units.anchor: Do not enter unpublished, proprietary or sponsor-restricted research information

units.why: Reproducibility rule: "keep records of prompts, versions and verification steps" in research: P62.
units.anchor: keep records of prompts, versions and verification steps

units.why: Defers to journal and publisher rules on disclosing AI assistance in scholarship: P62.
units.anchor: follow disciplinary norms and journal/publisher requirements for disclosure and citation of AI assistance

units.why: Software development section: generated code "may be insecure or incorrect", so review and test; verify AI output: P31.
units.anchor: Assume generated code may be insecure or incorrect. Perform code review, testing and security checks.

units.why: States the guidelines "must be read in conjunction with existing Clemson University policies, which remain controlling"; institutional framework: P56.
units.anchor: must be read in conjunction with existing Clemson University policies, which remain controlling

units.why: Binding rule: "must not enter Internal Use, Confidential or Restricted institutional data into publicly available generative AI tools": P50.
units.anchor: University employees, students and affiliates must not enter

units.why: IT Governance policy summary: all IT solutions "including generative AI tools and services" must be approved before use; vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: must be approved by the IT Governance team before the new IT solution

units.why: Quotes the Academic Catalog: graded works "generated by unauthorized AI" are "expressly forbidden"; students may not have AI produce graded work: P19.
units.anchor: generated by unauthorized AI (not authorized by the instructor/syllabus) or ghostwritten are expressly forbidden

units.why: Instructs users who shared sensitive data with an AI tool to "Report the incident"; a data-protection procedure: P50.
units.anchor: Report the incident

documents.title: Academic and Research AI Usage Quick Guide
documents.summary: A color-coded quick guide for students, instructors and researchers. It sorts uses into green, yellow and red, but all of it depends on course syllabus and instructor approval.
documents.stance_why: The guide says "always follow the requirements outlined in the course syllabus" and sorts uses into Green, Yellow and Red tiers whose permissions depend on instructors; with tiers and no single stance, it delegates.

units.why: Opening statement that AI "can support learning, discovery and innovation", with a focus on integrity; a purpose statement: P56.
units.anchor: Artificial intelligence tools can support learning, discovery and innovation across Clemson University

units.why: General rule to "always follow the requirements outlined in the course syllabus" and that those "take precedence"; the course or instructor sets the rule: P04.
units.anchor: always follow the requirements outlined in the course syllabus

units.why: "Regardless of the tools used, users remain responsible for the accuracy, integrity and originality of their final work": P29.
units.anchor: users remain responsible for the accuracy, integrity and originality of their final work

units.why: Student rule in the Green tier: "Only use AI in ways approved by instructors and in the syllabus", so unapproved use is out; this is the fallback when the syllabus does not allow it: P06.
units.anchor: Only use AI in ways approved by instructors and in the syllabus.

units.why: Students must "explain the process (what AI did vs. what the student did)"; understanding and explaining the work: P30.
units.anchor: Be prepared to explain the process (what AI did vs. what the student did).

units.why: Student rule to "Disclose/cite AI use when required": P24.
units.anchor: Disclose/cite AI use when required.

units.why: Green-tier example: brainstorming an outline when the instructor allows it: P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorming an outline if the instructor allows brainstorming tools.

units.why: Green example: feedback on "clarity/grammar of your own draft" with disclosure; writing support for prose: P18.
units.anchor: Getting feedback on clarity/grammar of your own draft (with required disclosure)

units.why: Green example: "Generating practice questions to study (not submitting as graded work)": P14.
units.anchor: Generating practice questions to study (not submitting as graded work).

units.why: Instructors "Set clear expectations for allowed uses of AI"; syllabus/assignment communication: P09.
units.anchor: Set clear expectations for allowed uses of AI

units.why: Instructors "Define prohibited uses of AI", communicating what is banned: P09.
units.anchor: Define prohibited uses of AI (e.g., full draft generation).

units.why: Instructors "Outline AI disclosure requirements for students", communicating disclosure expectations: P09.
units.anchor: Outline AI disclosure requirements for students.

units.why: Sample assignment instruction: AI for "outlining and grammar, but not for final answers" with a short statement; shows the rule set per assignment: P04.
units.anchor: AI may be used for outlining and grammar, but not for final answers

units.why: Researcher rule to follow journal, publisher or sponsor disclosure norms: P62.
units.anchor: Follow disclosure norms required by journals, publishers or sponsors.

units.why: Yellow-tier student rule: drafting graded content "Only if explicitly permitted"; permission is required first: P06.
units.anchor: Only if explicitly permitted.
units.policy: Drafting content that will be evaluated/graded is allowed only if explicitly permitted.

units.why: Yellow-tier student rule that disclosure or citation is mandatory where required: P24.
units.anchor: Must disclose/cite as required.

units.why: "The work must reflect the student's understanding" for AI-assisted graded content: P30.
units.anchor: The work must reflect the student's understanding.

units.why: Yellow example allows AI code snippets "only if the course allows it and students can explain how it works", an AI-code permission with conditions: P16.
units.anchor: only if the course allows it and students can explain how it works

units.why: Instructors must "Clarify what students may do (outline vs. draft vs. final)", separating stages of use: P09 (stating expectations).
units.anchor: Clarify what students may do (outline vs. draft vs. final).

units.why: Instructors specify disclosure details "(tool name, how used)"; citation detail requirements: P25.
units.anchor: Specify what must be disclosed (tool name, how used).

units.why: Example: AI summarization allowed if students attach "a reflection describing how they verified it"; reflections submitted: P26.
units.anchor: requiring students to attach a reflection describing how they verified it

units.why: Red tier: prohibited uses "may constitute academic misconduct or research noncompliance and can result in serious consequences"; misconduct classification: P36.
units.anchor: may constitute academic misconduct or research noncompliance and can result in serious consequences

units.why: Red tier student item: submitting AI-generated work as original "when not authorized": P19.
units.anchor: Submitting AI-generated work as original work when not authorized.

units.why: Red tier lists "Failing to disclose AI use when disclosure is required" as prohibited, making nondisclosure the violation: P28.
units.anchor: Failing to disclose AI use when disclosure is required.

units.why: Red example: copy-pasting AI output into graded work "without permission or disclosure"; AI producing submitted work: P19.
units.anchor: Copy/pasting AI output into a graded assignment without permission or disclosure.

units.why: Red example naming code: "Presenting AI-generated code as original work when not allowed": P19.
units.anchor: Presenting AI-generated code as original work when not allowed.

units.why: Red tier for instructors: "Leaving expectations ambiguous in ways that encourage policy violations"; failing to state expectations: P09.
units.anchor: Leaving expectations ambiguous in ways that encourage policy violations.

units.why: Red tier instructor item banning grading that conflicts with integrity requirements; no type covers instructor consistency in applying integrity rules, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Allowing grading practices that conflict with stated integrity requirements.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors must not grade or penalize inconsistently with their stated AI/integrity rules.

units.why: Red tier researcher item prohibiting entering unpublished or sponsor-restricted research data into public tools: P62.
units.anchor: Entering unpublished, proprietary, or sponsor-restricted research information into unapproved/public AI tools.

units.why: Red tier researcher item prohibiting misrepresenting authorship or skipping required disclosure: P62.
units.anchor: Misrepresenting authorship or failing required disclosure of AI assistance.

documents.title: Clemson Graduate School Statement on Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity
documents.summary: A Graduate School initial statement, explicitly not a policy, requiring instructors to put an AI section in their syllabi and route suspected violations to the Academic Integrity process. It gives a template where each instructor picks permitted, conditional or prohibited, and cautions against relying on AI detectors.
documents.stance_why: The statement says it is "rather than a policy" and tells instructors to choose "(permitted/permitted under certain conditions/prohibited)" in their syllabi, so it delegates with three options.

units.why: Puts "responsibility" on instructors and advisors to "clearly communicate their policy on the use of AI", leaving the policy to them: P04 for who decides, but the duty to communicate fits P09.
units.anchor: clearly communicate their policy on the use of AI in teaching and research

units.why: Instructors "should include a section in their syllabi addressing AI" with a clear policy on acceptable uses; a syllabus AI statement requirement: P09.
units.anchor: course instructors should include a section in their syllabi addressing AI

units.why: Syllabi should state that "suspected violations ... will be facilitated using the Academic Integrity process"; AI violations go through integrity processes: P36.
units.anchor: suspected violations of said policy will be facilitated using the Academic Integrity process

units.why: Advisors "should meet with advisees" to communicate the Research Misconduct policy; research and scholarship rules: P62.
units.anchor: advisors should meet with advisees to clearly communicate the University’s Research Misconduct policy

units.why: Tells instructors to "review the University's Artificial Intelligence Guidelines" before writing the syllabus section; advising faculty to learn about AI before setting policy: P63.
units.anchor: review the University’s Artificial Intelligence Guidelines for an overview of AI risks and best practices

units.why: Says "improper use negatively impacts student learning and the generation of original and creative thought"; AI use that shortcuts learning: P41.
units.anchor: improper use negatively impacts student learning and the generation of original and creative thought

units.why: The statement is "an initial statement ... rather than a policy" and future approaches "may transform"; it says the position is provisional: P54.
units.anchor: rather than a policy

units.why: Guiding principle: submissions "must either be students' own work or must clearly acknowledge the source"; students own what they submit: P29.
units.anchor: must either be students’ own work or must clearly acknowledge the source

units.why: Principle that students "must be able to demonstrate understanding of the content": P30.
units.anchor: Students must be able to demonstrate understanding of the content and/or intellectual contributions.

units.why: The syllabus template has instructors choose among "permitted/permitted under certain conditions/prohibited" for GAI/LLM; named categories of use: P05.
units.anchor: (permitted/permitted under certain conditions/prohibited)

units.why: If use is permitted, the syllabus should state "the need for attribution or not and specific citation formats"; disclosure rules set in the syllabus: P24.
units.anchor: expectations regarding the need for attribution or not and specific citation formats

units.why: Sample clause: students "may be asked to verbally explain or defend that content" and it counts in grading; oral checking of understanding: P34.
units.anchor: may be asked to verbally explain or defend that content

units.why: Sample clause: GAI/LLM "only permitted on assignments identified as an 'AI Assignment'"; rule set per assignment: P04.
units.anchor: only permitted on assignments identified as an “AI Assignment.”

units.why: Sample clause: students "retain records of their original work as proof that AI was not used"; keeping drafts/logs: P26.
units.anchor: retain records of their original work as proof that AI was not used

units.why: Sample clause: output "may provide biased and/or inaccurate results" and students must check; verify AI output: P31.
units.anchor: responsible for ensuring that your work does not replicate these biases or factual errors

units.why: Faculty are warned that Turnitin's AI detection "can produce false positives and should be used with some caution"; detector reliability: P39.
units.anchor: this software can produce false positives and should be used with some caution

units.why: Cites peers recommending detectors "not be used as a basis for academic dishonesty allegations": P39.
units.anchor: recommended they not be used as a basis for academic dishonesty allegations

units.why: Factual warning that Turnitin "will flag Grammarly edited content as AI-generated", showing detector error: P39.
units.anchor: Turnitin will flag Grammarly edited content as AI-generated.

documents.unit: Office of Teaching Effectiveness and Innovation
documents.title: AI Statements for Syllabi
tiers: AI Tools Permitted under NO Circumstances
AI Tools Permitted in Certain Circumstances
AI Tools Permitted for Course Work
AI Tools Integrated into the Course
documents.summary: Sample syllabus statements from the teaching center for four levels of AI use, from none to integrated. Faculty are told they need not follow them and the statements share documentation, understanding and integrity-process language.
documents.stance_why: The document offers "four levels of AI use statements varying from no use of AI to full use of AI" and says "faculty are not required to follow these recommendations", so it delegates with tiers.

units.why: States "faculty are not required to follow these recommendations"; instructors write their own AI statements: P04.
units.anchor: faculty are not required to follow these recommendations when creating their own AI syllabi statements

units.why: Offers "four levels of AI use statements varying from no use of AI to full use of AI"; named tiers: P05.
units.anchor: four levels of AI use statements varying from no use of AI

units.why: Lists elements each example gives, including "A rationale for why this class policy was chosen"; a recommended syllabus component: P09.
units.anchor: A rationale for why this class policy was chosen

units.why: Tier 1 text bans AI "under any circumstances, even with proper documentation and citation": P01.
units.anchor: under any circumstances, even with proper documentation and citation

units.why: Gives the reason for the ban: skills "are meant to come from your thinking and effort, not AI"; AI shortcuts practice that builds skill: P41.
units.anchor: meant to come from your thinking and effort, not AI

units.why: Violation concerns "will be reviewed fairly through the appropriate university academic integrity process": P36.
units.anchor: reviewed fairly through the appropriate university academic integrity process

units.why: Tier 2: AI permitted in certain circumstances, with students "informed in writing as to when, where, and how"; per-assignment rule: P04.
units.anchor: informed in writing as to when, where, and how these tools will be permitted

units.why: "Outside of these circumstances, AI tools should not be used", the default when no permission is given: P06.
units.anchor: Outside of these circumstances, AI tools should not be used for your work.

units.why: Where AI is allowed, use "must be documented and cited": P24.
units.anchor: Your responsible use of AI tools must be documented and cited

units.why: Students "must be able to demonstrate understanding of the content of any work submitted": P30.
units.anchor: you must be able to demonstrate understanding of the content of any work submitted

units.why: Tier 3 says AI "is permitted for work in this course", a permissive default with conditions: P02.
units.anchor: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools is permitted for work in this course.

units.why: Students "are accountable for the responsible, ethical use of these tools": P29.
units.anchor: you are accountable for the responsible, ethical use of these tools

units.why: Tier 4: AI "is integrated into the work for this course", so AI is built into the work: P02 (default permits and expects use).
units.anchor: integrated into the work for this course

units.why: Tier 4 says outcomes "include developing your ability to use these tools effectively"; teaching AI use as a skill: P44.
units.anchor: learning outcomes include developing your ability to use these tools effectively

notes: Coder A. Collect file lists no school/computing documents; course layer deferred. CCIT duplicate of guidelines not coded. Two units UNCOVERED (pressure-to-cheat support; consistent grading by instructors).
